help.decisions: usage: fleet-switchboard decisions [-h] [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--tier {cos,human,orchestrator,all}] [--json] [--fresh] [--watch] [--from SENDER] {list,escalate,batch,supersede,resolve,answer} ... Decisions have tiers. An orchestrator never goes straight to you: it raises a decision to the Chief of Staff (`report question` and the awaiting-cos label), which resolves it with your standing orders or escalates it (the awaiting-user label). `decisions [list]` prints the open ones: the issues with either label, the permission requests and questions of every fleet agent, and the questions and blocks workers reported that nobody has answered. The view depends on who asks (you are identified by your pane): the Chief of Staff sees every repo and tier; an orchestrator its own repo, every tier; anyone else only the human tier. --repo and --tier override. It says which view it printed. By default it reads decisions.json, which the daemon rewrites when the list changes; a file older than 120 s is said to be stale, never shown as current. `escalate`, `resolve` and `answer` are for the Chief of Staff (or you, in a plain shell). positional arguments: {list,escalate,batch,supersede,resolve,answer} list The open decisions in your view (the default) escalate Move a decision to the owner (the awaiting-user label, or at once for a permission request or question). Not judged batch Raise related findings as ONE decision: one issue in your own repo, labelled for the Chief of Staff, one row per finding supersede Mark several open decisions superseded by one issue. An issue decision: a comment and both labels off; a report: your `send` to its worker. Judged like `resolve` resolve Take both awaiting labels off a decision's issue: it is settled. Judged against the Chief of Staff's standing orders answer Answer an agent's pending permission request (allow|deny) or question (the answer's text) through v2, or a batch (--as-recommended, --row). Judged against the Chief of Staff's standing orders options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --repo OWNER/REPO Only this repo's decisions --tier {cos,human,orchestrator,all} Only this tier: cos, human or orchestrator; all for every tier --json Emit the list as JSON (with `stale` and `view`) --fresh Derive the list now instead of reading the file --watch Redraw when the list changes, until Ctrl-C (a fallback for a terminal without the TUI plugin) --from SENDER Lab only: the caller's fleet name

help.heavy: usage: fleet-switchboard heavy [-h] [--slots SLOTS] [--wait-max WAIT_MAX] [--name NAME] ... `heavy [--slots N] [--wait-max SECONDS] [--name WHO] -- <command...>`: waits for a free slot (default 3, config `heavy.slots`; one line every 30 s says who holds them), then runs the command as `taskpolicy -b <command>` (else `nice -n 10`) with its stdin, stdout, exit status and signals passed through. After --wait-max seconds (default 1800) it exits 75 and does not run the command. positional arguments: command -- <command...> options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --slots SLOTS How many commands may run at once (default: config heavy.slots, else 3) --wait-max WAIT_MAX Give up after this many seconds without a slot: exit 75 (default 1800) --name NAME Who the slot is held for (default: FLEET_HEAVY_NAME, the OpenCode session id, the user)

help.install: usage: fleet-switchboard install [-h] [--opencode OPENCODE] [--no-service] [--no-herdr-link] [--shared-profile] [--profile DIR] [--gh-user NAME] [--dry-run] [--uninstall] Idempotent. Each step says done, already done, or skipped (why). Finds an OpenCode v2 binary (never assumes `opencode` is v2), writes the config keys that are missing, puts the kit's agents, skills and plugins into a private v2 profile (never the directory your ordinary OpenCode reads, unless --shared- profile), links the herdr plugin, installs a service that keeps the daemon alive, then starts the daemon and prints `status`. No secret is written anywhere. options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --opencode OPENCODE The OpenCode v2 binary (absolute path); default: the configured one, then the known places --no-service Do not install the service --no-herdr-link Do not link herdr's plugin (it starts the daemon whenever herdr starts) --shared-profile Put v2's pieces in the directory your ordinary OpenCode reads too (~/.config/opencode), which can break a v1 OpenCode that reads them. Default: a private profile --profile DIR The private profile's directory (absolute); default: $XDG_DATA_HOME/fleet-switchboard/profile --gh-user NAME The gh account the agents' token comes from (default: gh's active one) --dry-run Print every step; write nothing --uninstall Reverse the profile pieces, the herdr link and the service; config, state and sessions stay

help.job: usage: fleet-switchboard job [-h] {start,status} ... A restart can kill a background run silently. `job start NAME -- COMMAND...` runs it detached in its own session and records it under the shared temp dir (or $FLEET_JOBS_DIR); `job status NAME` prints one line: alive, finished (with its exit code and the result file) or dead (killed, no exit code). A job found dead that nobody asked about is reported once to its starter's boss. positional arguments: {start,status} start Start a command detached and record it status One line: alive, finished (exit code, result file) or dead (killed, no exit code) options: -h, --help show this help message and exit

Default: read from the brief's CHECKPOINT line, if it can be --overdue WHEN Wake --reports-to at this time if the worker has not reported since the launch (60m, or an ISO time with a zone) --brief-file BRIEF_FILE The first prompt: a file, or - for stdin
help.notice: usage: fleet-switchboard notice [-h] [--from SENDER] {pr,withdraw,ack} pr [note ...] `notice pr` records a heads-up about a PR for the person's Decisions panel: information, not a decision. It sends no message and wakes nobody. Send it as soon as you OPEN the PR, so it is seen while CI and review run. It stays until the PR is merged or closed; sending it again refreshes the note. A number that is not an OPEN pull request is refused when you send it (an unreadable lookup never blocks). `notice withdraw <pr>` removes a notice (the agent that sent it, or its boss); a notice whose PR cannot be read for an hour is dropped. positional arguments: {pr,withdraw,ack} `pr` records a notice; `withdraw` removes the one for a PR (its sender or its boss); `ack` (you, in a plain shell) drops an order heads-up by its id pr The pull request: owner/repo#N or its URL (an issue, a number that is not an open PR, is refused) note Optional: one line of why, or what you intend (at most 300 characters) options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --from SENDER Lab only: the sender's fleet name
help.orders: usage: fleet-switchboard orders [-h] [--cos] {list,add,remove} ... The owner's standing orders live in the charter issue's `## Standing orders` section on GitHub, one per bullet: `- <text> (ordered by <name>, <YYYY-MM- DD>)`. The switchboard re-supplies them to every agent of the charter at its start, after each compaction and when they change, and the policy judge reads them at every tool call. `list` is open to anyone. `add` and `remove` are for the chief-of-staff only (you are identified by your pane); they edit only that section of the issue body. `--cos` prints the Chief of Staff's OWN standing orders: one local markdown file the owner edits (nothing here writes it). positional arguments: {list,add,remove} list The charter's standing orders, numbered add Chief of Staff only: record one standing order the owner gave remove Chief of Staff only: remove one order the owner revoked options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --cos PR 18: print the Chief of Staff's own standing orders file and its path (read-only: the owner edits that file in an editor; there is no write command)

help.report: usage: fleet-switchboard report [-h] [--issue ISSUE] [--all] [--from SENDER] {done,failed,blocked,question,working,paused,withdrawn} text [text ...] Tell the agent you report to what happened, in one line (at most 300 characters; detail goes on GitHub). `done`, `failed`, `blocked` and `question` are attention reports: delivered now, by the rule `send` uses. `working`, `paused` and `withdrawn` are progress reports: they ride in the next message to your boss and never wake it by themselves. `withdrawn` takes back your open question or blocked report on the ask (--all: on every ask) because it no longer stands. positional arguments: {done,failed,blocked,question,working,paused,withdrawn} What happened text One line: what happened (at most 300 characters) options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --issue ISSUE The issue the report is about (default: your own) --all With `withdrawn`: withdraw every open question or blocked report of yours, on any ask --from SENDER Lab only: the sender's fleet name
